name: 穆罕默德·安瓦尔·萨达特

points.title: 童年成长
points.description: 萨达特出生于埃及米尼亚省的一个贫苦家庭，是13个孩子中的第13个。他的父亲是埃及人，母亲是苏丹人。在尼罗河上游的农村环境中长大，这段经历塑造了他对埃及农村问题的深刻理解。萨达特在伊斯兰学校接受早期教育，后进入开罗的军事学院。这段贫困的童年经历培养了他对不平等的敏感性和对埃及民族独立的渴望。
points.descriptionEn: Sadat was born in a poor family in Minya Governorate, Egypt, the 13th of 13 children. His father was Egyptian and his mother was Sudanese. Growing up in a rural environment along the Nile River, this experience shaped his deep understanding of Egypt's rural problems. Sadat received early education in Islamic schools before entering the Cairo Military College. This impoverished childhood nurtured his sensitivity to inequality and his desire for Egyptian national independence.

points.title: 军旅生涯
points.description: 萨达特从军事学院毕业后加入埃及军队，成为一名军官。在开罗期间，他与纳赛尔等志同道合的军官组建了自由军官组织，秘密策划推翻君主制。二战期间，他曾因与轴心国有联系而被英国人短暂监禁。这段军旅生涯使他积累了军事经验，也让他建立了广泛的人脉网络，为后来的政变奠定了基础。1942年，他因参与反英活动被开除军籍，但1950年恢复军职。
points.descriptionEn: After graduating from military college, Sadat joined the Egyptian army as an officer. In Cairo, he formed the Free Officers Organization with like-minded officers including Nasser, secretly plotting to overthrow the monarchy. During World War II, he was briefly imprisoned by the British for his connections with the Axis powers. This military career provided him with valuable experience and extensive connections, laying the foundation for the later coup. In 1942, he was expelled from the army for anti-British activities but was reinstated in 1950.

points.title: 革命与执政
points.description: 1952年7月，萨达特参与领导了自由军官组织发动的革命，成功推翻了法鲁克国王，建立了埃及共和国。革命后，他担任了多个重要职位，包括议会主席、伊斯兰事务部长和副总统。在纳赛尔担任总统期间，萨达特虽然处于次要地位，但积累了丰富的政治经验。1967年六日战争失败后，埃及陷入困境，纳赛尔去世后，萨达特于1970年10月成为埃及总统。这一阶段奠定了他政治生涯的基础，也让他认识到埃及需要新的战略方向。
points.descriptionEn: In July 1952, Sadat participated in leading the revolution organized by the Free Officers, successfully overthrowing King Farouk and establishing the Egyptian Republic. After the revolution, he held several key positions including Speaker of Parliament, Minister of Islamic Affairs, and Vice President. During Nasser's presidency, Sadat, though in a secondary position, accumulated extensive political experience. After Egypt's defeat in the 1967 Six-Day War and Nasser's death in 1970, Sadat became President of Egypt in October 1970. This period laid the foundation for his political career and made him realize Egypt needed a new strategic direction.

points.title: 政治转向
points.description: 萨达特上台后推行了一系列被称为'纠正革命'的政策，包括释放政治犯、开放言论自由、推行经济自由化。他打破了苏联对埃及的垄断影响，开始寻求与西方建立更紧密的关系。1973年10月，他发动了第四次中东战争（又称赎罪日战争），虽然军事上未能取得决定性胜利，但政治上成功打破了以色列不可战胜的神话，提升了埃及的国际地位。这场战争为后来的和平谈判创造了条件，也巩固了萨达特在国内的领导地位。
points.descriptionEn: After taking office, Sadat implemented a series of policies known as the 'Corrective Revolution,' including releasing political prisoners, allowing greater freedom of speech, and promoting economic liberalization. He broke Egypt's monopoly dependence on the Soviet Union and began seeking closer ties with the West. In October 1973, he launched the Fourth Arab-Israeli War (also known as the Yom Kippur War). Although militarily inconclusive, it politically shattered the myth of Israel's invincibility and enhanced Egypt's international standing. This war created conditions for later peace negotiations and consolidated Sadat's domestic leadership.

points.place: 耶路撒冷、华盛顿、戴维营
points.title: 和平之旅
points.description: 1977年11月，萨达特做出了震惊世界的决定——访问以色列，成为第一位访问以色列的阿拉伯国家领导人。他在以色列议会发表演讲，呼吁和平解决阿以冲突。随后在美国总统卡特的斡旋下，他与以色列总理贝京于1978年在美国戴维营签署了《戴维营协议》。1979年3月，双方正式签署《埃以和平条约》，结束了两国长达30年的战争状态。这一历史性决策使萨达特获得了诺贝尔和平奖，但也导致埃及被阿拉伯联盟开除，并在国内引发强烈反对。
points.descriptionEn: In November 1977, Sadat made a world-shattering decision by visiting Israel, becoming the first Arab leader to do so. He addressed the Israeli Knesset, calling for peaceful resolution of the Arab-Israeli conflict. Subsequently, with mediation from U.S. President Carter, he and Israeli Prime Minister Begin signed the Camp David Accords in 1978. In March 1979, they formally signed the Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty, ending 30 years of war between the two countries. This historic decision earned Sadat the Nobel Peace Prize but led to Egypt's expulsion from the Arab League and strong domestic opposition.

points.title: 遇刺与遗产
points.description: 萨达特的和平政策和与以色列的关系在国内引发了强烈反对，尤其是伊斯兰极端分子的不满。1981年10月6日，在庆祝第四次中东战争8周年的阅兵仪式上，萨达特被伊斯兰圣战组织的成员刺杀身亡。他的遇刺反映了埃及社会内部的深刻分歧。尽管如此，萨达特的历史性决策——与以色列和平共处，为中东地区的和平进程开辟了新道路。他的经济开放政策也为埃及的现代化发展奠定了基础。萨达特被安葬在开罗的无名战士纪念碑旁，象征着他为埃及国家利益所做出的牺牲。
points.descriptionEn: Sadat's peace policies and relations with Israel sparked strong domestic opposition, particularly from Islamic extremists. On October 6, 1981, during a military parade celebrating the 8th anniversary of the 1973 war, Sadat was assassinated by members of the Islamic Jihad organization. His assassination reflected deep divisions within Egyptian society. Nevertheless, Sadat's historic decision to make peace with Israel opened new paths for the Middle East peace process. His economic liberalization policies also laid the foundation for Egypt's modern development. Sadat was buried at the Unknown Soldier Memorial in Cairo, symbolizing his sacrifices for Egypt's national interests.

supporter.zh: 萨达特被视为埃及现代史上最具远见和勇气的领导人之一。他敢于打破常规，冒着巨大风险推动和平进程，结束了埃及与以色列的长期敌对状态。他的经济开放政策为埃及引入了外资和技术，促进了国家现代化。萨达特的政治勇气和外交智慧使他成为中东和平进程的关键人物，为该地区带来了稳定与发展的可能性。他的'纠正革命'也为埃及的政治生活注入了新的活力。
supporter.en: Sadat is regarded as one of the most visionary and courageous leaders in modern Egyptian history. He dared to break conventions and took enormous risks to advance the peace process, ending the long-standing hostility between Egypt and Israel. His economic liberalization policies attracted foreign investment and technology, promoting Egypt's modernization. Sadat's political courage and diplomatic wisdom made him a key figure in the Middle East peace process, bringing stability and development possibilities to the region. His 'Corrective Revolution' also injected new vitality into Egypt's political life.

critic.zh: 批评者认为萨达特的决策过于冒险和机会主义，牺牲了阿拉伯团结原则。他与以色列的和平条约使埃及被阿拉伯世界孤立，失去了地区影响力。他的经济政策虽然引入了外资，但也导致了贫富差距扩大和社会不公。萨达特被指责为独裁者，压制政治反对派，并过度依赖西方支持。他的遇刺部分源于国内政策的不平衡，未能有效解决埃及面临的社会经济问题，最终导致政治不稳定。
critic.en: Critics argue that Sadat's decisions were overly risky and opportunistic, sacrificing the principle of Arab solidarity. His peace treaty with Israel isolated Egypt from the Arab world and diminished its regional influence. While his economic policies attracted foreign investment, they also led to widening income inequality and social injustice. Sadat is accused of being a dictator who suppressed political opposition and relied excessively on Western support. His assassination was partly due to the imbalance in his domestic policies, which failed to effectively address Egypt's socioeconomic challenges, ultimately leading to political instability.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，萨达特被视为一个复杂而矛盾的历史人物。他既是民族英雄，也是争议人物；既是和平缔造者，也是政治冒险家。他的历史地位因中东和平进程的长期影响而得到肯定，但也因国内政策的失败而受到质疑。萨达特的形象在埃及社会两极分化，一些人视他为解放者，另一些人则视他为背叛者。他的生平故事成为研究中东政治转型、外交决策和民族认同的重要案例。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Sadat is viewed as a complex and contradictory figure. He is simultaneously a national hero and a controversial figure; both a peacemaker and a political adventurer. His historical legacy is affirmed by the long-term impact of the Middle East peace process, yet questioned by the failures of his domestic policies. Sadat's image remains polarized in Egyptian society, with some seeing him as a liberator and others as a traitor. His life story has become an important case study for studying Middle Eastern political transformation, diplomatic decision-making, and national identity.

self.zh: 任何不寻求和平的人，就是寻求战争。
self.en: Anyone who doesn't seek peace is seeking war.

others.zh: 萨达特是一位勇敢的领导人，他愿意冒着一切风险来实现和平，即使这意味着与自己的同胞对抗。
others.en: Sadat was a courageous leader who was willing to risk everything to achieve peace, even if it meant going against his own people.
